description_full: Liquidity Services, Inc. provides e-commerce marketplaces, self-directed auction listing tools, and value-added services in the United States and internationally. The company operates through GovDeals, Retail Supply Chain Group, Capital Assets Group, and Machinio & Software Solutions segments. It provides solutions that enable government entities and commercial businesses to sell surplus property and real estate assets through GovDeals, Bid4Assets, and Sierra marketplaces. The company also offers surplus management, asset valuation, asset sales, marketing, returns management, asset recovery, and ecommerce services; and operates marketplaces to sell excess, returned, and overstocked consumer goods. In addition, it operates Machinio marketplace, a global search engine platform for listing used equipment for sale in the construction, machine tool, processing, transportation, printing, agriculture, and laboratory/medical sectors. Further, the company provides Machinio System platform that offers website hosting, email marketing, and inventory management to equipment sellers, as well as auction platform services to entrepreneurs and businesses. Additionally, it operates an online auction marketplaces comprising Invaluable, a global marketplace for fine art, antiques, jewelry, and collectible; and AuctionZip, a U.S.-focused marketplace and directory for local and regional auctioneers. The company also provides auction houses with private-label auction websites, auction-management software, marketing services, and integrated payment processing; and offers buyers managed shipping and subscription access. It offers its products to consumer electronics, general merchandise, apparel, scientific equipment, aerospace parts and equipment, technology hardware, real estate, energy equipment, industrial capital assets, heavy equipment, fleet and transportation equipment, and specialty equipment. Liquidity Services, Inc. was incorporated in 1999 and is based in Bethesda, Maryland.

financial_summary: Liquidity Services, Inc. is a small-cap consumer cyclical business with a $1.1B market cap on $478M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +15% over the past three years and +6% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

Returns on capital run at 13% against a 10% cost of capital, a 3-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it. Gross margins of 50% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $49M in free cash flow — roughly 10 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.55× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.0× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 40× is fortress-like.
Shareholder yield is only 0.1%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 25% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

sect: Its 10% operating margin is roughly in line with the Consumer Cyclical median (8%).

The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 385 companies in the universe; the top four hold 25% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 49% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 16% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 26% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 40% and a beta of 1.02, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 1.80 vs 5y 1.03), so read it loosely.
About $10.4M trades a day, enough to build a position, and interest is running hot at 1.9x its yearly average volume.

val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $22.90 (margin of safety -54%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 9%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $10.35 to $50.99 (P10-P90).
On multiples it looks expensive against Consumer Cyclical peers: P/E 34.5 vs 18.7, EV/EBITDA 16.2 vs 11.0 and P/FCF 22.7 vs 16.5 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 11% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 4.4% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 5.4% (vs the 8% bar).
The 2 covering analysts target $51.00 on average, 45% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 13% earns above the cost of capital of 9.6%, but the 3pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 5.23).
It runs a 50% gross margin and converts 10% of revenue into free cash flow, or 6% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 1.55x.
ROE of 15% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.7x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 8pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 3.9% of revenue on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $225.2M (20% of market cap).
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 6.1, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 15.0% over 3 years, 13.2% over 5 years and 5.9% over 10 years, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 20%).
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 12.9% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded -4.1% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (0.9x, 1.9% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 19, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own 24.7%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 83%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (14 sales, net $682K sold).
Shareholder yield is a modest 0.1% (0.1% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 2.5% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 818 employees, each generates about $584K of revenue, 1.5x the Consumer Cyclical median, and revenue has grown 2.6% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $60K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
CEO pay is $1.2M (2x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (2/10, lower is better).
